item.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.31807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang

item.title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.
item.dc:creator: Pham The Nhan

item.title: An Exposition of Gerstenhaber's Proposition 1: Elimination of Coboundaries in Formal Deformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gerstenhaber's foundational work on formal deformations of associative algebras relates the first non-trivial term of a deformation to the second Hochschild cohomology group. In the proof of Proposition~1 of his 1964 paper, a leading Hochschild $2$-cocycle which is a coboundary is successively removed by formal changes of variables. If this elimination terminates after finitely many steps, no limiting argument is required, but the possibility that coboundaries continue to be eliminated indefinitely is left largely implicit in the original treatment. This expository note makes that limiting argument fully explicit for deformations over $K[[t]]$ of a fixed associative $K$-algebra $A$. We use the $t$-adic topology on the relevant spaces of formal power series and formal endomorphisms, establish completeness and the continuity of composition, inversion and the action on formal multiplications, and show that an infinite sequence of successive changes of variables assembles into a single, well-defined formal equivalence. This yields a complete, self-contained proof of the classical result and its rigidity consequence.
item.dc:creator: Rinkila Bhutia, Zuiner Jamir

item.title: Semirings Induced by Semilattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.32271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate semirings induced by join-semilattice (meet-semilattices) with a degenerate multiplication on all the subset that excludes the multiplicative unity. The way those semirings are defined enables a big impact of the semilattices we start with on the associated semirings: many of their order-theoretic properties reflect in algebraic properties of the induced semirings. This enabled constructing examples of semirings with desired properties as well as providing counterexamples to wrong claims in old and recent papers/preprints. In particular, we construct families of examples of semirings induced by non-modular join-semilattices for which the lattice of subtractive ideals is non-modular disproving a claim of Henriksen who introduced this important class of ideals of semirings.
item.dc:creator: Jawad Abuhlail

item.title: Commutator syzygies and pure resolutions over central polynomial rings with division-ring coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.32272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring and let $A=D[x,y,z]$ with central indeterminates. For positive integers $p,q$ and $a,b\in D$, put $f=x^p+az^p$ and $g=y^q+bz^q$. We compute their left syzygy module and the minimal graded free resolution of $A/(Af+Ag)$. This quotient has projective dimension two if $ab=ba$ and three otherwise. In the latter case, it has finite length and total Betti numbers $(1,2,2,1)$, with a pure resolution of type $(0,d,3d,4d)$ when $p=q=d$. These tables do not occur over polynomial rings over fields. If $D$ is finite-dimensional over its center $K$, the Betti tables of modules of finite length over $K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and left modules of finite length over $D[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ generate the same rational cone for every $n\ge1$. In three variables, the semigroup over $K$ is properly contained in that over $D$ when $D$ is noncommutative.
item.dc:creator: Hoang Anh Tu, Huynh Viet Khanh

item.title: Similarity classes of $5\times5$ matrices over local rings of length two
item.description: arXiv:2611.32387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative local principal ideal ring of length two whose residue field has arbitrary characteristic. Prasad, Singla and Spallone classified similarity classes in $M_n(R)$ for $n\leq4$ by using module extensions. We extend their classification to $n=5$. We determine explicit extension-orbit representatives and stabilizers for the partitions $(3,2)$, $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,1,1,1)$. We prove that every orbit contains exactly one of the listed representatives. Together with the known primary cases, these results give all similarity classes in $M_5(R)$ and their centralizers. We also determine representatives and stabilizers for the family $(m+1,1,1,1)$ for every $m\geq1$. When the residue field is finite, we obtain the sizes and total number of similarity classes.
item.dc:creator: Himadri Mukherjee, Gunja Sachdeva, Adeep Varghese

item.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.
item.dc:creator: Muratova Kh. A., Tyan M. D

item.title: The socle of the last term in a minimal injective resolution II
item.description: arXiv:2611.32486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R$ be a Gorenstein ring with left and right self-injective dimensions $n$. We prove that the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $_RR$ has an essential socle. It answers an open question of Iwanaga and Sato. As a consequence, we get that for any left $R$-module $M$ with injective dimension $n$, the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $M$ also has an essential socle.
item.dc:creator: Zhaoyong Huang, Tiwei Zhao

item.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.
item.dc:creator: Beaudoin Simon, Bonnefoy Quentin, Marrani Alessio, Rausch de Traubenberg Michel, Saulquin Victor

item.title: Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.32871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.
item.dc:creator: Liran Shaul

item.title: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
item.description: arXiv:2611.33066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojt\v{e}ch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.
item.dc:creator: Peter Jipsen, Erkko Lehtonen, Reinhard P\"oschel

item.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.31443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.
item.dc:creator: Ross Glew, Pavlo Pylyavskyy

item.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.31963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$. This holds for rectangular matrices over an arbitrary field, and unifies and extends the known results that $k = 1$ suffices for rank-one coefficients (Lov\'asz, 1989; Ivanyos, Karpinski, and Saxena, 2010) and that $k = 2$ suffices for skew-symmetric coefficients of rank two (Oki and Soma, 2025). We present two applications. First, if $r$ is a constant, then the nc-rank of an $n \times n$ linear symbolic matrix can be computed by a randomized algorithm with $O(m n^2 + n^\omega)$ arithmetic operations over a sufficiently large field, where $\omega$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Second, the hierarchy of polytopes introduced by Hirai (2026), which converges to the nc-independent set polytope, stabilizes at the $r$-th level; this is based on a counterpart of our main result for the degree of the Dieudonn\'e determinant.
item.dc:creator: Yuni Iwamasa

item.title: The standard generators of the tetrahedron algebra and their look-alikes
item.description: arXiv:2405.05504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The tetrahedron algebra $\boxtimes$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra defined by generators $\{x_{ij} \mid i, j \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}, i \neq j\}$ and some relations, including the Dolan-Grady relations. These twelve generators are called standard. We introduce a type of element in $\boxtimes$ that ``looks like'' a standard generator. For mutually distinct $h, i, j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, consider the standard generator $x_{ij}$ of $\boxtimes$. An element $\xi \in \boxtimes$ is called $x_{ij}$-like whenever both (i) $\xi$ commutes with $x_{ij}$; (ii) $\xi$ and $x_{hk}$ satisfy a Dolan-Grady relation. Pick mutually distinct $i,j,k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$. In our main result, we find an attractive basis for $\boxtimes$ with the property that every basis element is either $x_{ij}$-like or $x_{jk}$-like or $x_{ki}$-like. We discuss this basis from multiple points of view.
item.dc:creator: Jae-Ho Lee

item.title: Higher-power inverse functional identities and Frobenius collision obstructions
item.description: arXiv:2607.09669v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $D$ be a division ring, let $n\geq 2$, and let $f,g:D\to D$ be additive maps satisfying $f(x)x^{-1}+x^n g(x^{-1})=0$ for every nonzero $x\in D$. We establish general vanishing criteria, give an explicit classification over finite fields, and determine the additive-polynomial solutions over infinite fields of positive characteristic. If $\mathbb{F}_q\subseteq Z(D)$, every additive map $D\to D$ admits a canonical decomposition into $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$-weight components, and the identity pairs precisely the weights $r,s$ satisfying $r+s\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Consequently, for $q=p^m$, the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the solution space is the number of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $0\leq i,j<m$ satisfying $p^i+p^j\equiv n+1\pmod{q-1}$. Over an infinite field of characteristic $p>0$, the additive-polynomial solutions are exactly the sums of paired Frobenius terms with $p^i+p^j=n+1$. This classification concerns additive-polynomial maps and does not assert a classification of arbitrary additive maps. Prime-field dilation gives complete vanishing in characteristic zero and, in characteristic $p>0$, whenever $p-1$ does not divide $n-1$. In characteristic two, we prove complete vanishing for $n=2$ on every noncommutative division ring. More generally, when $[D:Z(D)]=\infty$, every solution vanishes if the center is infinite. If the center is the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, the same conclusion holds for $2\leq n\leq q-1$. The remaining cases are stated explicitly.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Algebra Combinatorics Discrete Structures and Applications (2026)
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Aliabadi

item.title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.09849v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.
item.dc:creator: Wen Teng, Ripan Saha

item.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
item.description: arXiv:2611.18541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \Theta_2, \dots$ with $\Theta_k \circ \Theta_j = \Theta_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $\Theta_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. Without freeness the answer reverses: FL(3) contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices, so the lattice analogue of Takahasi's chain condition for free groups fails. The theorem itself is checked by the Agda proof assistant under its safe flags, for free lattices over generators with decidable equality, and its formal proof uses no classical principle: finite searches and an induction on a finite set replace the infinite pigeonhole principle by which a chain yields a coherent chain.
item.dc:creator: William DeMeo, Ralph Freese

item.title: The standard filtration of Leavitt path algebras and topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on

item.title: From n-systems to Lie and Courant algebroids
item.description: arXiv:2512.03391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces a method for constructing pure algebroids, dull algebroids, and Lie algebroids. The construction relies on what we call $n$-systems on vector bundles, and we provide explicit formulas for all resulting structure maps. Analogously, metric $n$-systems defined on metric vector bundles allow us to construct metric algebroids, pre-Courant algebroids, and Courant algebroids.
item.dc:creator: Liqiang Cai, Zhuo Chen, Zhixiong Chen, Yanhui Bi

item.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
item.description: arXiv:2610.11013v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\delta=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $$ f=(x+\delta t,y+\delta z,z,t) $$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $Z[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted. We also prove that the Freudenburg--Moser-Jauslin involution $$ \tau(a,b,x,y)= \bigl(b,a,-b^3x+(1+ab+a^2b^2)y,(1-ab)x+a^3y\bigr). $$ of $F[a,b,x,y]$ is tame over every field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, and list an explicit factorization in Appendix.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Ivan Shestakov
